newly_closed: membership in the actual localized relative denominator is equivalent to coordinatewise divisibility by the selected finite Smith coefficients
the finite Smith filtration D(s) is characterized by divisibility only on coordinates not yet adjoined
for i not in s, the historical scalar quotient D(s) / D(insert i s), interpreted as D(s).colon D(insert i s), is exactly the principal ideal generated by e_i without any ordering hypothesis
the scalar quotient D(s) / G1-star is exactly the infimum of the remaining principal coefficient ideals
that infimum is a single displayed principal ideal only under an explicit greatest-remaining-divisor hypothesis, rather than an unproved ordering of Mathlib's selected Smith coefficients
the same scalar quotient formulas hold after adjoining an arbitrary common finitely supported identity tail, and hence for the countable Nat-indexed zeta-tail specialization
the printed distinguished-coefficient chain is available with its missing divisibility premise visible in the theorem type
limitations: The historical slash is formalized as Mathlib's scalar colon ideal A.colon (B : Set E), not as the additive quotient B/A. The unconditional one-step formula is proved for the actual finite localized Smith pair and for the freely adjoined common identity-tail model. Quotienting a filtration stage by the whole ground module is generally an infimum of remaining principal ideals; its simplification to one displayed (e_i) requires the explicit hypothesis that every remaining coefficient divides e_i. Mathlib's selected Smith coefficients are not shown here to be canonically ordered, normalized, unique, or choice-independent. The free Finsupp tail is not independently identified with the historical unbounded zeta module. No resultant, determinant norm, primitive normalization, infinite determinant, infinite product, or later elimination stage is asserted.
